candidates.title: Establishment, Modification, and Revocation of Class E Airspace; Alaska, AK
candidates.raw_excerpt: This action supplements a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published by the FAA in the Federal Register on June 17, 2025, which proposed to establish Class E domestic en route airspace (Class E6) within a designated landmass and within 12 miles from a designated shoreline associated with the state of Alaska to facilitate the vectoring of instrument flight rules (IFR) aircraft on direct routes where the current en route structure is insufficient or improper within the proposed airspace areas. As revised in this SNPRM, the FAA now proposes to establish five discrete areas of Class E domestic en route airspace over the state. Due to redundancy, the NPRM also proposed to remove two Class E6 airspace areas and modify 101 Class E airspace areas extending upward from at least 700 feet or more above the surface of the earth (Class E5) to remove any portion extending upward from 1,200 feet above the surface. This SNPRM continues to propose these actions, but also now proposes to remove two Class E airspace areas extending upward from 1,200 feet above the surface, revoke a duplicate Class E5 airspace legal description, and redefine airspace areas from a "Point of Origin" instead of using their respective airport reference points. Finally, both the NPRM and this SNPRM propose administrative amendments to the legal descriptions of 101 Class E5 airspace areas that would correct or update nomenclature as needed. This action would support IFR operations while enhancing the safety and management of aircraft operations within the National Airspace System (NAS).

candidates.raw_excerpt: Gambling addicts aren’t the only ones being taken for a ride by prediction markets. As gambling platforms like Polymarket and Kalshi become have more popular than ever before, financial criminals are also using prediction markets to unleash fraud and graft on an unprecedented scale. According to the Wall Street Journal , this phenomenon was identified as far back as February, when a payment processing company contracted by Polymarket flagged a massive rise in bets made with stolen debit cards. Essentially, fraudsters began by plugging stolen financial information into the prediction market to make wagers. If they won, the perpetrators would then withdraw the funds, syphoning them into alternative payment methods under their control. As the WSJ reports, criminals tried to make off with at least $10 million using this method — causing the third-party payment processor to reject over 80 percent of its incoming transactions as fraudulent, which is vastly over the industry norm of around 1 percent. Following what has arguably become the business model of the day , the WSJ revealed that Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan essentially told his horrified compliance team to keep raking in the cash and deal with the consequences when they come — if they ever come at all, that is. Financial policy experts say the level of graft on display is without parallel. As Joe Konizeski, a former attorney for the Commodity Future Trading Commission put it, “in the regulated space, this kind of thing does not happen.” “You have adults who handle customer funds and make sure they’re sourced appropriately and handled appropriately,” Konizeski continued. Few tech executives have acknowledged these urgent harms. Instead they’re choosing to push a narrative around the hypothetical threat of a runaway “superintelligence” which humans can no longer control. That’s why it’s notable that Jensen Huang, CEO of the AI chipmaking titan Nvidia, was recently grilled on the cognitive harm AI is inflicting on students. Unfortunately, his response was far from reassuring, providing further proof of the AI industry’s blatant disregard for the wellbeing of ordinary people. Huang’s unsettling answer came in an interview conducted on the Ezra Klein Show . Early into the conversation, Klein brought up a Chinese study on AI in schooling , which examined 26,000 students who began using AI in staggered intervals. Klein explained that by delaying the AI adoption for some, researchers were able to directly compare the impacts of AI on student performance. Though students were able to complete work faster with AI, the study found compelling evidence that the cognitive skills needed to complete school work melted away, resulting in lower exam scores in the long-term. The deal is expected to close in mid-2027 for ~$54 per Iridium share—in a mix of cash and RKLB stock.  Gotta have it: The Iridium purchase is the latest in a string of increasingly large buyouts that started before the company went public via SPAC in 2021. The new satellite coincides with the regional operator’s 50 th anniversary. ARABSAT-50 will be a high-power Ku-band satellite designed to provide immediate and effective sustainability to support and ensure the continuity of Direct-to-Home (DTH) television broadcasting services at the 26 degrees East orbital position. The General category may only retain, possess, or land large medium and giant (i.e., measuring 73 inches (185 centimeters (cm) curved fork length (CFL) or greater) BFT when the fishery is open. This action also waives the previously scheduled restricted-fishing days (RFDs) for the remainder of the September time period. With the RFDs waived during the closure, fishermen aboard General category permitted vessels and HMS Charter/Headboat permitted vessels may tag and release BFT of all sizes, subject to the requirements of the catch-and- release and tag-and-release programs. On October 1, 2026, the fishery will reopen automatically and previously scheduled RFDs for the October through November time period will resume.

candidates.title: Expedition 75 astronauts continue science work as Crew-13 readies for launch
candidates.raw_excerpt: AS the International Space Station continues to orbit Earth as it has for over a quarter of a century, the Expedition 75 astronauts aboard have been busy performing science and maintenance tasks, and preparing for new arrivals and a crew handover early next month. Just before the end of August, the Cygnus XL cargo ship S.S. Steven R. Nagel reboosted the Station to prepare for the upcoming Progress MS-35 cargo flight, which at the time was scheduled to fly on Sept. 9. Following on from three spacewalks made from the US segment of the ISS in August , another EVA was carried out on Sept. 1. Sophie Adenot, as EV1 with red stripes on her space suit, and Jessica Meir, as EV2, conducted US EVA-99, returning to the Station’s Quest airlock module after six hours and 49 minutes outside. The astronauts installed a new retroreflector on the Harmony node module’s forward port to support navigation for visiting vehicles. Sophie Adenot outside the ISS during EVA-99. (Credit: ESA/NASA) Adenot and Meir also replaced a high-definition camera on the Station’s truss assembly and swabbed the Station’s exterior for microorganism samples. The astronauts began installing jumper cables for electrical systems and started work on replacing the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer’s radiator assembly, tasks that will be finished on a future spacewalk. During the spacewalk, Sophie Adenot experienced mobility issues in her left shoulder, which were traced to a joint heater harness getting caught in the shoulder joint. Meir unzipped the joint, which appeared to solve the issue. Various issues with the aging Shuttle-era suits have delayed Station spacewalks and forced repairs on various suit parts, which can be returned to Earth aboard Cargo Dragon spacecraft for evaluation and maintenance if required. EVA-99 was the 248th spacewalk overall in support of the ISS , and marked Meir’s seventh and Adenot’s third spacewalk. candidates.title: Disney's Ludwig Von Drake was inspired by rocket scientists 65 years ago
candidates.raw_excerpt: Did you know that the first character that Walt Disney created to specifically appear on television was inspired, in part, by early Space Age rocket scientists? On this day 65 years ago (September 24, 1961), Disney introduced the "renowned scientist, lecturer, psychologist [and] world traveler," Ludwig Von Drake. A member of the Duck family (he is the "brilliant and eccentric" uncle of Donald Duck), Von Drake was "the outstanding genius of the century" (per Disney himself) who helped to explain scientific principles and technological concepts to the millions of people who tuned in every Sunday to watch Walt Disney's Wonderful World of Color on NBC. A few years later, after expertly (but often absent-mindedly) addressing topics such as how color television works, the health benefits of exercising, and the history of aviation, Von Drake dove into the topic for which he said he wrote the book on, in the February 10, 1963, episode "Inside Outer Space." candidates.title: Google Gearing Up to Launch Experimental “Data Center” Into Space Next Week
candidates.raw_excerpt: It’s not just Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin looking to send data centers into orbit. Google is also looking to get in on the fun — and is now gearing up to launch a fridge-sized satellite with the equivalent computing power of a single server as soon as next week. As the New York Times reports , the prototype satellite is part of the tech giant’s Project Suncatcher. As its name suggests, the goal is to take advantage of unfiltered sunlight around the clock to power AI data centers in our planet’s orbit — instead of crushing the electrical grid , spewing copious amounts of pollution , and draining fresh water supplies back on the ground. Companies like Google still have a long way to go to find out whether it actually works, let alone whether it’s financially feasible. Obstacles include errant pieces of space junk that could turn enormous orbital data centers into Swiss cheese, copious amounts of space radiation wreaking havoc on the onboard electronics — which also have to be kept cool somehow — and providing a solid enough connection with the surface hundreds of miles below. That’s not to mention the extremely complicated and likely costly process of maintaining these servers. Human technicians can wander into a data center facility to swap out parts, but servicing satellites would be infinitely more complex. Orbital data centers are no panacea to our terrestrial data center woes, either. Experts warn that massive constellations could be incredibly ecologically damaging , releasing copious amounts of atmospheric pollution and risking damage to the ozone layer. For now, technicians at Google are stress-testing the first Project Suncatcher experimental satellite in a lab, ahead of loading it onto a SpaceX Falcon 9 for launch on October 1.
